order_note: After SQL 142 (its predecessor, applied in production 2026-11-05), which it supersedes: the file requires SQL 142's two policies (aws_insert_mortgage_companies_tenant_admin, aws_update_mortgage_companies_tenant_admin) in SQL 142's exact form and replaces them. SQL 143 (owner decisions 2026-11-05: "Remove should delete it. It can always be added again later, anyone can do this, mortgage agents should be able to share and edit list", then "1" = delete only when unused) needs public.mortgage_companies (uuid id, boolean is_active), public.claims, public.loss_draft_tracking and public.check_cases (each a uuid mortgage_company_id), public.aws_is_authenticated(), public.aws_is_cross_tenant_reader(), public.aws_has_any_tenant_membership(), public.aws_is_active_mortgage_agent(uuid), auth.uid() and the roles authenticated and checksops (spec prerequisites). The applying login must own public.mortgage_companies (altered_relations_owned_by_login: CREATE POLICY and CREATE TRIGGER need the owner). The engine's read-only catalog counts must each be 1 before any apply: mortgage_companies_rls_enabled (file: sql143_table_missing, sql143_rls_disabled), mortgage_companies_id_uuid_is_active_boolean (file: sql143_column_missing), mortgage_company_references_uuid (file: sql143_reference_missing), mortgage_companies_owner_policy_intact (aws_write_mortgage_companies PERMISSIVE FOR ALL TO exactly {authenticated}, aws_is_authenticated() AND aws_is_cross_tenant_reader(); file: sql143_owner_policy_missing, sql143_owner_policy_collision), mortgage_companies_sql142_policies_replaceable (SQL 142's two in SQL 142's form, or on a re-run absent with the file's three present; file: sql143_sql142_policy_collision, sql143_sql142_policy_missing), mortgage_companies_no_unexpected_policy (file: sql143_unexpected_policy) and mortgage_company_references_readable_by_login (the login, which owns the in-use guard, reads claims, loss_draft_tracking and check_cases past row level security: owner without FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, or superuser / BYPASSRLS, with SELECT; file verify: sql143_guard_cannot_see_all_rows). The file also raises sql143_function_missing without the three helper functions. It creates public.aws_can_edit_mortgage_company_directory() (SECURITY DEFINER sql, EXECUTE authenticated and checksops) and public.aws_mortgage_company_in_use_guard() (SECURITY DEFINER plpgsql, row_security off, EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC, authenticated and checksops), the trigger aws_mortgage_company_in_use_guard BEFORE DELETE OR UPDATE OF id FOR EACH ROW, and three PERMISSIVE policies TO authenticated on (aws_can_edit_mortgage_company_directory() AND is_active): aws_insert_mortgage_companies_member FOR INSERT, aws_update_mortgage_companies_member FOR UPDATE, aws_delete_mortgage_companies_member FOR DELETE; it drops SQL 142's two. Deactivating and reactivating stay with aws_write_mortgage_companies (platform owner only), which is not changed; its deletes are guarded by the same trigger. The pre-state after SQL 142 is derivable: SQL 142's two policies as SQL 142 created them and nothing of SQL 143 (c62a1b0b337cca713cd8551f1a1c70f507ef451e40731baa6e8479abae51038d, derived by aws/tests/release-sql143-executor.test.mjs and read back on PostgreSQL 16). If the read-only inspect finds SQL 143's state as intended it reports already_applied true and nothing is applied. Changes no other policy, grant, RLS flag, table, column or row; the API allowlist (write-allowlist.mjs) still decides which columns a write may carry.
